batch_metadata.description: Lyrical and abstract works exploring the sensory experience of the Archive and the ancestral memory of the herd.

books.title: Sonnets from the Ivory Desk
books.author: Elara Greyverse
books.summary: A collection of fourteen-line poems exploring the intersection of archival silence and the passage of time. The sequence focuses heavily on the physical decay of vellum and the scent of old ink.
books.notes: Greyverse was a contemporary of Lila Trent and a frequent visitor to the Eastern Stacks.

books.title: The Infrasound Odes
books.author: Silas Probink
books.summary: Experimental verse intended to be read aloud, mimicking the low-frequency communication of the herd. The poems explore themes of distance, seismic connection, and ancestral calls across the Grey Marches.
books.notes: Includes a controversial preface on the 'acoustics of memory.'

books.title: Wrinkles in the Verse
books.author: Vira Mammorlyric
books.summary: A series of lyrical meditations on the texture of elephantine skin as a metaphor for historical record. Each poem corresponds to a specific era of the Tusklands, from the Founding Age to the Modern Era.
books.notes: Mammorlyric's work is often cited in Stratum V fables as a source of moral inspiration.

books.title: Dust Mote Haiku
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: Minimalist poetry capturing the movement of light and dust within the Archive's reading rooms. The collection emphasizes the beauty of the overlooked and the weight of the microscopic.
books.notes: Authorship is attributed to a rotating group of junior archivists.

books.title: The Supertusker's Song
books.author: R. Tuskpoet the Elder
books.summary: An epic poem recounting the migration of a legendary bull across the Grey Marches during a period of great drought. It focuses on the isolation of leadership and the burden of the first step.
books.notes: Considered the poetic companion to Temberton's Border Wars Trilogy.

books.title: The Trunk's Lament
books.author: B. Pachydermus
books.summary: A collection of elegies written during the Great Drought of the 18th century. The poems focus on the loss of ancestral waterholes and the heavy silence that fell upon the herd.
books.notes: Pachydermus was a survivor of the drought; his work is considered a primary emotional record of the era.

books.title: Ivory Echoes
books.author: L. Greymane
books.summary: Modernist free verse exploring the resonance of sound within the Archive's vaulted ceilings. The author uses seismic metaphors to describe the weight of history and the vibration of memory.
books.notes: Greymane was a student of H.L. Pruett and often applied archival theory to her poetic structures.

books.title: The Grey Migration
books.author: S. Tuskwell
books.summary: An epic poem detailing the first crossing of the Tusklands. It emphasizes the rhythmic nature of the march and the collective memory of the path as a sacred text written in the dust.
books.notes: Tuskwell's use of 'Dust-as-Ink' metaphors became a staple of later Grey Reformation literature.

books.title: Stomp and Silence
books.author: V. Ivoryn
books.summary: A series of short, percussive poems designed to be performed with rhythmic footfalls. The work explores the duality of physical presence and archival absence in the modern era.
books.notes: Includes performance notes for 'Seismic Recitation.'

books.title: The Archivist's Quatrains
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Found in the margins of a Stratum I tragedy, these quatrains describe the daily ritual of dusting the shelves. The identity of the author remains a subject of intense scholarly debate.
books.notes: Often attributed to the Archivist of Hall Seven, though the meter differs significantly.

books.title: Seismic Verses
books.author: Dr. G. Footfall
books.summary: Poetry that attempts to translate infrasonic communication into written meter. The collection is noted for its unusual use of white space to represent pauses in the herd's call.
books.notes: Footfall was a pioneer in 'Acoustic Ontology.'

books.title: The Vellum Veil
books.author: Elara Greyverse
books.summary: A later work by Greyverse focusing on the tactile sensation of handling ancient records. The poems treat the Archive as a living organism with its own breath and pulse.
books.notes: Written during Greyverse's self-imposed isolation in the Lower Stacks.

books.title: Odes to the Great Bull
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: A rare poetic excursion by the court dramatist. These odes celebrate the virtues of strength and memory in the founding leaders of the Tusklands.
books.notes: Scholars believe these were commissioned for the centennial of the Founding Age.

books.title: The Dust of Ages
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: A collaborative sequence of poems where each stanza was written by a different archivist over a period of fifty years. It captures the slow accumulation of time within the library walls.
books.notes: The original manuscript is kept in the staff lounge of Hall Seven.

books.title: Tusk and Twilight
books.author: Silas Probink
books.summary: A collection of evening poems meant to be read as the light fades in the reading rooms. The work explores the transition from the clarity of day to the shadows of the stacks.
books.notes: Probink's most accessible work, often found in the Archive's gift shop.

books.title: Marginalia of the Forgotten
books.author: T. Trumpscribe
books.summary: Poems constructed entirely from notes written in the margins of discarded manuscripts. The collection treats these fragmentary voices as a chorus of the overlooked.
books.notes: Trumpscribe spent thirty years cataloging margin notes before compiling this work.

books.title: The Proboscis Hymns
books.author: M. Elaphtongue
books.summary: Religious verse celebrating the trunk as a sacred tool of exploration and connection. Each hymn corresponds to a different gesture of greeting or comfort.
books.notes: Elaphtongue was a theologian who sought to codify the spiritual significance of touch.

books.title: Whispers in the Wrinkles
books.author: Vira Mammorlyric
books.summary: A late-career work using irregular line breaks to mimic the patterns of aged skin. The poems meditate on how trauma and joy both leave their marks.
books.notes: Critics note the increasingly fragmented structure as reflecting Mammorlyric's own advancing age.

books.title: The Silent Frequency
books.author: Dr. P. Dermwave
books.summary: Poetry that attempts to render infrasound visible through typographic manipulation. The verses explore communication that exists below the threshold of conscious hearing.
books.notes: Dermwave was a physicist before becoming a poet, bringing acoustic theory to his craft.

books.title: Dust Psalms
books.author: R. Greymantle
books.summary: Devotional poetry treating archival dust as a sacred substance containing the essence of all written words. Each psalm addresses a different aspect of preservation and decay.
books.notes: Greymantle served as a minor archivist and saw his work as a form of prayer.

books.title: The Ivory Cycle
books.author: H. Tuskweaver
books.summary: A seasonal sequence of sonnets mapping the growth and wear of tusks across a lifetime. The poems parallel ivory's journey with the accumulation of personal history.
books.notes: Tuskweaver's only published work, compiled posthumously by his students.

books.title: Seismic Lullabies
books.author: N. Pachyrock
books.summary: Contemporary verse that imagines the earth's vibrations as a mother's song to her calf. The collection blends geological imagery with intimate moments of care.
books.notes: Pachyrock's debut, winner of the Grey Marches Poetry Prize.

books.title: The Silence Between Shelves
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: Poems about the negative space in the Archive, the gaps where books once stood. The work focuses on absence as a form of presence.
books.notes: Each poem was written in response to a specific empty shelf location.

books.title: Trunk Root Sonnets
books.author: E. Proboscian
books.summary: Formal sonnets that trace etymological connections between words related to touch and memory. The sequence explores language as a physical act.
books.notes: Proboscian was both a linguist and a poet, often annotating his own work extensively.

books.title: The Weight of Pages
books.author: L. Mammorpress
books.summary: Poems that calculate the physical mass of books as a metaphor for the burden of knowledge. Each piece includes the actual weight of the volume it references.
books.notes: Mammorpress worked as a bookbinder and brought precise measurements to her poetry.

books.title: Grey Thunder Odes
books.author: B. Stormtusk
books.summary: Odes written during thunderstorms, attempting to capture the overlap between weather and the herd's rumbling calls. The poems use storm imagery to explore collective emotion.
books.notes: Stormtusk claimed to only write when lightning was visible from the Archive's windows.

books.title: Fragments of the First Migration
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Incomplete verses found carved into stone markers along the ancient migration route. The fragments hint at a longer epic now lost to erosion and time.
books.notes: Compiled by the Archaeological Society of the Grey Marches from field research.

books.title: The Cartographer's Verse
books.author: S. Tuskline
books.summary: Poetry that treats landscape features as stanzas in a larger geographic text. Each poem corresponds to a specific location in the Grey Marches, creating a lyrical map.
books.notes: Often consulted by travelers alongside traditional maps for its evocative descriptions.

books.title: Ink and Ivory
books.author: T. Pachwrites
books.summary: Ekphrastic poems responding to illuminated manuscripts in the Archive's collection. The work explores the relationship between image and text, decoration and meaning.
books.notes: Pachwrites had special access to the Rare Manuscripts Room for this project.

books.title: The Murmur Underneath
books.author: Dr. G. Footfall
books.summary: Late career poems that visualize seismic readings as verse. The work treats earthquakes and footsteps as part of a continuous conversation with the earth.
books.notes: Footfall's final work before his death; includes actual seismographic printouts as illustrations.

books.title: Ancestral Hums
books.author: V. Herdwhisper
books.summary: Poems structured as family trees, with each generation represented by a different stanza form. The work explores how memory changes as it passes through time.
books.notes: Herdwhisper interviewed dozens of matriarchs to compile the genealogies referenced.

books.title: The Archive Breathes
books.author: Elara Greyverse
books.summary: Greyverse's final collection, treating the library as a living being with respiration and pulse. The poems anthropomorphize dust, air currents, and the creak of wood.
books.notes: Published posthumously from manuscripts found in Greyverse's study.

books.title: Pachyderm Pastorals
books.author: W. Greenpasture
books.summary: Pastoral poems reimagining the harsh landscape of the Grey Marches as an idealized paradise. The work contrasts the brutality of survival with moments of unexpected beauty.
books.notes: Greenpasture never visited the Grey Marches; the work is based entirely on archival accounts.

books.title: The Dust Remembers
books.author: M. Particulate
books.summary: Prose poems that imagine dust particles as carriers of memory from every book they've touched. Each piece follows a single mote's journey through the Archive.
books.notes: Particulate worked as an Archive cleaner for twenty years before publishing this collection.

books.title: Tusk Song Variations
books.author: R. Tuskpoet the Younger
books.summary: Thirty-three variations on a single four-line poem about ivory growth. Each variation explores a different poetic form while maintaining the core imagery.
books.notes: The younger Tuskpoet was the grandson of R. Tuskpoet the Elder and sought to honor his legacy.

books.title: Echoes in the Vaulted Hall
books.author: L. Greymane
books.summary: A sequel to Ivory Echoes, focusing specifically on the reverberation patterns in Hall Seven. The poems use repetition and echo to create sonic texture.
books.notes: Greymane conducted acoustic experiments in the Hall to inform the structure of these poems.

books.title: The Wrinkled Text
books.author: P. Dermscript
books.summary: Concrete poetry arranged on the page to resemble the folds and creases of elephantine skin. The visual layout is as important as the words themselves.
books.notes: Dermscript was influenced by the avant-garde movements of the early twentieth century.

books.title: Silence as a Verb
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: An experimental collection that treats silence as an action rather than an absence. The poems use extensive white space and minimal text.
books.notes: Some pages contain only a single word; others are completely blank with titles only.

books.title: The Footfall Chronicles
books.author: N. Pachyrock
books.summary: Poetry based on interviews with pilgrims walking the ancient migration routes. The verses capture the rhythm of long-distance travel and the stories shared along the way.
books.notes: Pachyrock walked 500 miles gathering material for this collection.

books.title: Marginalia in Red Ink
books.author: T. Trumpscribe
books.summary: A companion volume to Marginalia of the Forgotten, focusing exclusively on angry or dissenting margin notes. The poems preserve the voices of forgotten critics.
books.notes: Trumpscribe's final work, completed just before his death.

books.title: The Hum of Memory
books.author: Silas Probink
books.summary: Meditative poems exploring the persistence of sound in the mind long after it has ceased. The work uses repetition to create a sense of ongoing resonance.
books.notes: Probink described these as 'poems to be heard rather than read.'

books.title: Ivory Splinters
books.author: K. Tuskbreaker
books.summary: Short, sharp poems about loss and injury. The fragmentary form mirrors broken tusks and the sudden violence that creates them.
books.notes: Tuskbreaker lost a tusk in battle; this collection emerged from that experience.

books.title: The Archivist's Hours
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Poems marking the passage of time through the daily routines of archive work. Each piece corresponds to a different hour of the working day.
books.notes: Found in a locked drawer in the Chief Archivist's desk in 1809.

books.title: Subterranean Verses
books.author: Dr. P. Dermwave
books.summary: Poetry about the layers beneath the Archive's foundation. The work imagines the building as the tip of a much deeper structure extending into the earth.
books.notes: Dermwave consulted geological surveys while writing this collection.

books.title: The Call Across Distance
books.author: V. Herdwhisper
books.summary: Poems structured as messages sent across vast distances through infrasonic call. The collection explores separation, longing, and the faith required to send a message into emptiness.
books.notes: Written during Herdwhisper's self-imposed exile in the Eastern Stacks.

books.title: Dust Light Haiku
books.author: M. Particulate
books.summary: Minimalist observations of how afternoon light illuminates dust in the reading rooms. Each haiku captures a specific moment of visibility and disappearance.
books.notes: Particulate kept a journal of dust observations for fifteen years before publishing this selection.

books.title: The Grey Matriarch's Song
books.author: L. Mammorvoice
books.summary: A long dramatic monologue in the voice of a herd matriarch reflecting on leadership and mortality. The poem uses the metaphor of guiding the young to water.
books.notes: Mammorvoice performed this piece in the Archive's main hall to acclaim.

books.title: Seismic Elegies
books.author: B. Pachydermus
books.summary: A later collection of elegies commemorating specific individuals lost to the Great Drought. Each poem includes the date and location of the death.
books.notes: Pachydermus's final work, more personal and specific than his earlier collection.

books.title: The Bound and the Broken
books.author: T. Pachwrites
books.summary: Poems about the physical condition of books, from pristine first editions to volumes held together with string. The work treats damage as a form of biography.
books.notes: Pachwrites worked closely with the Archive's conservation department.

books.title: Trunk Root Ballads
books.author: E. Proboscian
books.summary: Narrative ballads telling folk stories of the Grey Marches through the lens of touch and physical connection. Each ballad centers on a specific gesture.
books.notes: Proboscian's late work, showing a shift from formal sonnets to narrative ballads.

books.title: The Archive at Night
books.author: S. Moonshade
books.summary: Poems about the Archive after hours, when the reading rooms are empty. The collection explores the building's secret life in darkness.
books.notes: Moonshade was a night watchman who wrote while making his rounds.

books.title: Wrinkle Maps
books.author: Vira Mammorlyric
books.summary: Mammorlyric's middle-period work treating facial wrinkles as geographic features. The poems read each fold as a valley or ridge in a landscape of experience.
books.notes: Includes hand-drawn diagrams mapping wrinkle patterns to actual geographic locations.

books.title: The Infrasonic Journal
books.author: Dr. G. Footfall
books.summary: A year-long poetic diary attempting to record daily infrasonic observations in verse. The entries blend scientific notation with lyrical reflection.
books.notes: Each entry is dated and includes frequency measurements.

books.title: Grey Stone Odes
books.author: R. Greymantle
books.summary: Odes to the stone architecture of the Archive itself. The poems treat the building's foundation as a sacred text written in granite.
books.notes: Greymantle consulted with the original architects' descendants while writing.

books.title: The Crossing Songs
books.author: S. Tuskwell
books.summary: Short poems meant to be recited during migration, marking the rhythm of the journey. Each song corresponds to a specific landmark or water source.
books.notes: Still used by some pilgrims who walk the traditional routes.

books.title: Silence Variations
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: Twelve variations on the theme of archival silence, each by a different member of the Collective. The work explores how different poets approach the same absence.
books.notes: Each variation maintains the same structure but radically different content.

books.title: The Ivory Relics
books.author: K. Tuskbreaker
books.summary: Elegies for tusks lost in battle, treating them as fallen warriors deserving commemoration. Each poem includes details of how the tusk was lost.
books.notes: Tuskbreaker interviewed dozens of veterans to gather stories for this collection.

books.title: The Weight of Ink
books.author: L. Mammorpress
books.summary: Poems about the physical act of writing, from grinding ink to the pressure of the quill. The collection treats writing as manual labor.
books.notes: Mammorpress ground her own ink and bound her own books throughout her career.

books.title: Thunder Across the Marches
books.author: B. Stormtusk
books.summary: Later storm poems focusing on the movement of weather systems across open land. The verses track clouds and rain with the precision of meteorological observation.
books.notes: Stormtusk kept detailed weather journals that informed these poems.

books.title: Ancestral Vibrations
books.author: N. Pachyrock
books.summary: Poems tracing family lineages through seismic memory rather than written record. The work imagines footfalls as a form of genealogical documentation.
books.notes: Pachyrock combines geological research with oral history interviews.

books.title: The Proboscis Sonnets
books.author: M. Elaphtongue
books.summary: Formal sonnets exploring the trunk as a tool of knowledge acquisition. Each poem addresses a different aspect of touch, from texture to temperature.
books.notes: Elaphtongue's secular work, in contrast to his earlier devotional hymns.

books.title: Dust on Dust
books.author: M. Particulate
books.summary: Philosophical poems considering dust as both subject and object, observer and observed. The work questions where the boundary lies between matter and meaning.
books.notes: Particulate's final collection, published two years before his death.

books.title: The Vellum Ghosts
books.author: Elara Greyverse
books.summary: Gothic poems imagining the spirits of animals whose skins became writing surfaces. The collection treats vellum as haunted material.
books.notes: Greyverse's most controversial work, condemned by some religious authorities.

books.title: The Migration Calendar
books.author: S. Tuskline
books.summary: A poetic calendar marking the traditional dates of migration departure and return. Each entry blends practical information with lyrical observation.
books.notes: Still consulted by traditionalists who follow the old migration patterns.

books.title: Wrinkled Wisdom
books.author: P. Dermscript
books.summary: Didactic poems treating age and experience as forms of accumulated knowledge. The work argues that wisdom is literally written on the body.
books.notes: Dermscript's most accessible work, often used in educational settings.

books.title: The Herd's Pulse
books.author: V. Herdwhisper
books.summary: Poems that attempt to capture the collective heartbeat of a moving herd. The verses use repetition to create a sense of synchronized rhythm.
books.notes: Herdwhisper's last published work before her death three years later.

books.title: Marginalia of Light
books.author: T. Trumpscribe
books.summary: A third collection from margin notes, this time focusing on decorative illuminations rather than text. The poems describe what the scribes drew in moments of distraction.
books.notes: Trumpscribe's middle work, less bitter than his later collection.

books.title: The Seismic Psalter
books.author: Dr. P. Dermwave
books.summary: Devotional poems treating earthquake activity as a form of divine communication. Each psalm responds to a specific recorded seismic event.
books.notes: Written during wartime, when Dermwave saw parallels between bombs and earthquakes.

books.title: Ivory Threshold
books.author: H. Tuskweaver
books.summary: Poems about the moment when a tusk first breaks through gum tissue. The work treats emergence and maturation as a continuous threshold.
books.notes: Rediscovered in the 1920s and recognized as Tuskweaver's masterwork.

books.title: The Archive Speaks
books.author: S. Moonshade
books.summary: A long dramatic monologue in the voice of the Archive itself, reflecting on the texts it houses. The poem personifies the building as a conscious entity.
books.notes: Moonshade's final work, published posthumously from his night-watch journals.

books.title: Grey Dawn Haiku
books.author: The Quill Collective
books.summary: Morning haiku written by archivists at the start of their shifts. Each poem captures the moment of transition from night to day in the reading rooms.
books.notes: A companion to Dust Mote Haiku, focusing on temporal rather than spatial moments.

books.title: Tusk Fracture Elegies
books.author: K. Tuskbreaker
books.summary: Clinical yet moving poems about tusk injuries and their treatment. The collection blends medical terminology with emotional reflection.
books.notes: Tuskbreaker consulted with military surgeons while writing this collection.

books.title: The Rumble Underground
books.author: Silas Probink
books.summary: Poems about sounds that travel through earth rather than air. The collection explores communication that bypasses conventional hearing entirely.
books.notes: Probink's middle-period work, bridging his early odes and late meditations.

books.title: The Archive's Skin
books.author: L. Mammorpress
books.summary: Poems treating the Archive's outer walls as a protective hide. The work parallels building maintenance with bodily care and grooming.
books.notes: Mammorpress's final collection, showing increasing concern with preservation.

books.title: Pastoral Thunder
books.author: B. Stormtusk
books.summary: A synthesis of Stormtusk's storm observations and pastoral traditions. The poems find moments of beauty and grace in violent weather.
books.notes: Stormtusk's final work, published the year before his death; considered his masterpiece.
